title: Studios explains when it builds, and what a partner gets on day one
summary: A new page argues that Studios should build only when a serious search finds no better-positioned builder, starting with the cheapest useful experiment.
text: Payment beats compliments as evidence, so Studios runs the cheapest useful test before it charters a company. The page lists what a partner starts with: a licensed rights position, operators who have carried an FDA submission or a large system replacement to the finish, a first buyer in reach, and a written exit path. It also says where ventures get built, how to engage, and the standard a proposal is measured against.
